root_cause: activeDefragAlloc() couples allocation-of-replacement with freeing-of-original into a single call. activeDefragHExpiresOB() retained a reference (keystr) into the original object's memory for use after that call, not realizing the original memory had already been released by the time it performed the dict lookup/update. The ordering of free vs. use was inverted: the free needed to happen only after all derived pointers from the old object were no longer needed.
findings: In activeDefragHExpiresOB(), `keystr` is captured as `kvobjGetKey(kvobj)` at the top of the function, i.e. it is a pointer into the memory owned by the original (pre-defrag) `kvobj` allocation. Later, the code calls `kvobj = activeDefragAlloc(kvobj)`. activeDefragAlloc() (see src/defrag.c, activeDefragAlloc) allocates a new copy of the object AND immediately frees the old pointer via zfree_no_tcac
